items.heading: A School Screening
items.text: A school screening is a hint, not a diagnosis. Colour vision deficiency comes in types and degrees, and recruiters treat a mild result and a strong one differently.

items.heading: This Table Records What
items.text: This table records what the documents we read say. Standards change, so use it to ask the right question and then read the recruiter's current notice.

rows: A quick plate or app check, often done once in a school health camp.
A hint only. It does not tell you the type, the degree or what a recruiter's board will decide.
Numbers hidden in dotted plates. Armed forces boards use it at the first stage, and the railway Station Master proforma lists it with the required result 'Normal'.
The test most recruiters name first, so ask for a result on paper from a doctor.
You name coloured signal lights at a set distance. A paper on Indian Air Force standards describes the Martin Lantern for pilot grading.
Matters for flying and signalling roles. Recruiters set their own pass mark.
A matching test that grades how strong the deficiency is. The armed forces colour perception guidelines, as quoted by the Delhi High Court, use it with Ishihara at appeal and review boards.
Where a case reaches a review board, this is the harder check. Ask an eye specialist whether it is available near you.
